prs.title: NBA WS2: probabilistic minutes and conserved opportunity; retain M0 benchmark
prs.body:
Future NBA exposure previously relied on a recent played-game median. This draft adds isolated M0/M1/M2 conditional-minute distributions, separate availability/participation semantics, a versioned `NBAOpportunityForecast/1.0.0` handoff, and a team allocation mechanism with exact 240+25×OT conservation and five-on-court witnesses.

The bounded chronological replay fits on 2023–24 and evaluates 25,641 matched appearances across 1,231 franchise games / 164 dates in 2024–25. M2 CRPS improves 3.9561 → 3.5533 (−10.18%; paired 97.5% date-cluster difference CI −0.4391 to −0.3717), while central-estimate MAE improves 5.2427 → 4.9878 minutes. Both challengers pass aggregate numerical gates, but **neither is adopted**: M2 90% coverage regresses on low-minute outcomes (80.7% → 72.3%) and inferred OT outcomes (77.1% → 68.0%). Retain M0 as benchmark. These outcome-conditioned stress rates are diagnostic, not unconditional coverage targets.

Source audit found 68 All-Star exhibition rows. A WS2-local franchise adapter excludes them before histories, with a complete ledger, disclosed post-initial-score integrity amendment, and preserved initial unfiltered evidence. Canonical collectors and WS1 schemas are untouched.

Validation: 25 WS2 tests pass locally and in a detached read-only Deepnote run; 34 existing NBA/population/phase-1.5 tests pass. A 1,000-scenario fixture has zero conservation/five-on-court violations, versus independent total error averaging 20.42 player-minutes. The final full replay takes 224.93 wall seconds / 357.1 MiB peak RSS; 100-player forecast inference is under one CPU second per model.

Participation FPR/FNR, teammate-absence effects, authentic market ablations and real prospective forecasts remain blocked by missing pregame candidate/availability/source receipts. The manual shadow CLI is exercised only with explicitly synthetic fixtures and retains rejected rows. No prop-probability, causal variance-attribution or economic-edge claim is made.

- Governing: `PA-V25-MASTER-2026-11-09 / v1.1`; current user authorizes this bounded WS2 shadow ticket.
- Status: implemented / tested / historical exploratory shadow; independent WS4 review pending. Not a trusted release.
- Preregistration: `975dc89`; fitting/scoring: `df22657`; final implementation: `0efd7d0`; base main: `912bc70`.
- Full report: `research/nba_ws2/REPORT.md`; pinned-source replay: `bash research/nba_ws2/reproduce.sh`.
- Hashes, matched predictions, failed/identity-excluded denominators and runtime receipts: `research/nba_ws2/results/evidence_manifest.json`.
- Deepnote notebook: `8c4c10b625ca4b4ea8635a9723f82ee9`; final test/report run: `22802efa-932c-4141-bdcc-b6a57797f329`.
- Protected boundaries: no canonical source collector, outcome likelihood, WS4 scoring infrastructure, frozen model, production decision, schedule or NUTS job changes.
- Rollback: remove the isolated WS2 module, its test file and research directory. No production imports exist.

Independent review should first challenge tail coverage, participation conditioning, source-time assumptions, competition identity filtering and the fact that simplex projection changes marginal minute laws. No merge or model promotion is requested by this draft.

Minimal shared CI has no pandas/scikit-learn. Four research-replay checks explicitly skip there; all 25 checks run locally and in Deepnote. The 21 core checks require only NumPy/SciPy. No CI or shared dependency configuration changed.

prs.title: NBA WS1: immutable pregame inputs, historical scope audit and source quarantine
prs.body:
The NBA population's recent stream stops at November 1, and its regular-season filter admits exhibition and NBA Cup championship games. This PR adds an isolated, immutable pregame source interface with explicit temporal rejection and scope quarantine, preserving the existing collectors, evaluator and archives.

Governing: PA-V25-MASTER-2026-11-09 / v1.1. Phase 0R/1 NBA WS1 infrastructure only; shadow-only, no statistical model or release approval.

Base: 912bc7010058092ea735dcda0aa941429194474b
Code/head: 53c01a9eabb9ed09b5c3186eae0d086b07bcc891
Warehouse read: 97a8bb566826afe5a3e5a7b8c632043d8a1dca24

### Implemented
- Versioned NBAPregameFeatureSnapshot, immutable receipts/records, deterministic hashes and strict deserialization with feature reconstruction.
- Prior player/team vectors, actual minutes/starts/attempts, explicit roster and injury uncertainty; separate original contract/game-market context.
- Same-game/future/late-source rejection, dated crosswalk resolution, versioned corrections and retained rejection denominators.
- Reuse of the existing ESPN parser; legacy population adapter requires explicit eligible game scope and retains provider namespaces.
- Coverage/missingness report, machine-readable quarantine/abstention ledger, raw-source pregame sample and precise WS2/WS3/WS4 handoff.

### Executed evidence
- Audited all 99 NBA shards: 2,249,104 rows, 204,464 player-games, 9,625 games; no structural/cross-stat identity or combo arithmetic failures.
- Quarantined 18 games / 3,938 rows: 15 exhibition games and three Cup championship games. Original data are unchanged. Recent November 1–14 population dates remain missing.
- Real Lakers–Suns November 15 pregame package: 36 roster memberships, 55 roster-associated historical player-games, ten retained responses. Freeze 19:02:12.757146Z; final serialization 19:09:58.797255Z; scheduled start 21:00Z.
- Sample hash a0532e8c6f26ea47102a9a6867f7c030c9914a79999d6124481066d779a4cf13; exact offline source-byte replay passes.
- Existing November 10 evaluator replay ran twice in read-only Deepnote, preserving NBA 250 / NHL 106 contracts, 712 sides, 1,314 attempts and 354 settlements. Output bytes SHA-256 b438345979353e9c421c440c9bd39f0202994a3e94925a5416b904279b0c617d. Run c4ca630e-64d3-47e5-bed4-cc00ac333f93.
- First Deepnote attempt rejected the parent settlement directory; the corrected invocation points to existing official_source_raw. No archived input was edited.

### Validation
25 WS1 tests passed; existing population suite 21 passed / three optional ArviZ/PyMC skips; evaluator 11 passed; official capture 13 passed. Total 70 passed, three skipped. Compilation and staged whitespace checks pass. Pytest was unavailable; unittest executed these suites. No numerical fitting was run.

Commands:
```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests/nba_ws1 -v
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_population*py' -v
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_v25_nhl_nba_phase1.py' -v
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_v25_official_capture.py' -v
python -m v2.nba_ws1.replay docs/nba_ws1/sample --expect-hash a0532e8c6f26ea47102a9a6867f7c030c9914a79999d6124481066d779a4cf13
```

### Open gates / review
Full independent league schedule reconciliation failed at the bounded ESPN range endpoint (HTTP 400). Original historical availability clocks, independent provider parity/corrections, dated cross-provider identity mapping, game-active eligibility, historical possessions/pace and original quote/payout evidence remain unavailable or incomplete. The sample is correctly BLOCKED for downstream forecasting. Hashes and passing tests do not establish full source certification.

Independent reviewer approval has not been performed; same-agent adversarial checks and separate-runtime evaluator replay are not independent code signoff. Please review docs/nba_ws1/INTERFACE.md, COVERAGE_REPORT.md, HANDOFF.md and STATUS_LEDGER.md.

### Preservation / rollback
Only v2/nba_ws1, tests/nba_ws1 and docs/nba_ws1 are added. No minutes/outcome model, production weights/ranking, evaluator, existing forecast/source archive, training pause marker or global schedule changes. No paid data, Actions dispatch or model refits. [skip ci] avoids automatic hosted workflow use; the relevant checks were executed as above.

Before merge, close this draft to roll back. After merge, revert this isolated commit and pin downstream opt-in adapters back first; preserve all original data. No deployment/migration or background process was introduced.
